preconditions.description: The input is a single integer n where 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() == [str(k)] + colors and len(colors) == n and all(1 <= int(c) <= k for c in colors)
postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is an integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ n) representing the minimum number of colors used. The second line contains n space-separated integers (colors) between 1 and k, where the i-th color corresponds to the (i+1)-th jewelry piece (price = i+2).

postconditions.expression: all(colors[i] != colors[j] for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if (prices[i] != prices[j]) and (prices[i] % prices[j] == 0 or prices[j] % prices[i] == 0) and is_prime_divisor(prices[i], prices[j]))
postconditions.description: For every pair of jewelry pieces (i, j) where one price is a prime divisor of the other, their colors must differ. Here, prices[i] = i + 2, and is_prime_divisor(a, b) is true if a is a prime divisor of b (i.e., a divides b and a is prime).
The number of colors k is the minimum possible for the given n, where min_possible_colors(n) is the smallest integer such that the coloring constraints are satisfied.

invariants.expression: all(1 <= int(c) <= k for c in colors) and len(colors) == n
invariants.description: The colors list must have exactly n elements, each between 1 and k (inclusive).
